tool_summary: Astral's fast Python package and project manager, increasingly displacing pip/pip-tools/virtualenv. Handles dependency installation, virtual environments, and script execution in one binary.
platform_notes: uv behavior is consistent across Linux and macOS.

rules.description: The run subcommand executes a Python script, auto-installing any dependencies declared via inline script metadata (PEP 723) first. This is a distinct execution vector from `uv pip install`: the script itself, and any dependency it pulls in, runs in one step with no separate review point between install and execution.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends entirely on the script's contents, which commandant does not inspect.

rules.description: The --index or --index-url flags point uv at a package index other than the default PyPI. Installing from an untrusted or unfamiliar index is a common supply-chain attack vector, since the installed package's build scripts run with the invoking user's privileges.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be uninstalled, but its install-time build scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: The pip install, add, or sync subcommands install packages, which can execute arbitrary build code with the invoking user's privileges.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be uninstalled, but install-time build scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Manages Python packages, virtual environments, or project dependencies. Read-only subcommands (pip list, tree, pip show) do not alter system state. Severity here reflects that unrecognized or future uv subcommands fall through to this rule; known read-only subcommands are not themselves being flagged as risky.
rules.notes: Default bumped to WARNING (not INFO) because this tool's CLI surface evolves quickly; an unmatched/unrecognized subcommand should surface for review rather than silently pass as benign.
